title: Kaufen, kaufen, kaufen (Shopping & Clothes)
description: Shop for clothes, ask about prices, hold a simple conversation in a shop, meet the accusative case, and make plans with friends.

notes.heading: Shops and Shopping — Geschäfte
notes.body:
First, the places where you buy things:

| German | English |
|---|---|
| das Geschäft | the shop |
| das Kaufhaus | the department store |
| die Bäckerei | the bakery |
| die Metzgerei | the butcher's |
| die Boutique | the boutique / clothes shop |
| der Markt | the market |
| das Einkaufszentrum | the shopping centre |

Useful verbs: **kaufen** (to buy), **einkaufen** (to go shopping — separable: *Ich kaufe am Samstag ein*), **kosten** (to cost).

💡 Example: *Am Wochenende gehen wir ins Einkaufszentrum.* — At the weekend we go to the shopping centre.

notes.heading: Clothes — die Kleidung
notes.body:
Learn each item with its article:

| German | English |
|---|---|
| die Hose | the trousers |
| das T-Shirt | the T-shirt |
| die Schuhe (pl.) | the shoes |
| der Pullover | the jumper |
| die Jacke | the jacket |
| das Kleid | the dress |
| der Rock | the skirt |
| die Mütze | the cap / beanie |
| die Jeans | the jeans |
| der Mantel | the coat |

💡 Worked example: *Im Winter trage ich einen Mantel und eine Mütze.* — In winter I wear a coat and a cap.

📎 Key point: the verb for wearing clothes is **tragen** (ich trage, du trägst, er/sie trägt — the a becomes ä for du and er/sie).

notes.heading: Prices and Money — Wie viel kostet ...?
notes.body:
The currency in Germany and Austria is **der Euro (€)**; one euro is 100 **Cent**.

Ask about a price with **Wie viel kostet ...?** (How much does ... cost?):

- *Wie viel kostet das T-Shirt?* — How much does the T-shirt cost?
- *Es kostet zwölf Euro fünfzig.* — It costs €12.50.

German says prices without the word "and": *drei Euro zwanzig* = €3.20.

More shopping words:

| German | English |
|---|---|
| billig | cheap |
| teuer | expensive |
| der Preis | the price |
| das Sonderangebot | the special offer |

💡 *Die Jacke ist zu teuer, aber der Pullover ist billig.* — The jacket is too expensive, but the jumper is cheap.

notes.heading: In the Shop — a Dialogue
notes.body:
A typical conversation in a clothes shop:

- **Verkäufer:** *Guten Tag! Kann ich Ihnen helfen?* — Good day! Can I help you?
- **Kunde:** *Ja, ich möchte eine Jacke.* — Yes, I would like a jacket.
- **Verkäufer:** *Welche Farbe?* — Which colour?
- **Kunde:** *Blau, bitte. Haben Sie die Jacke in Größe 38?* — Blue, please. Do you have the jacket in size 38?
- **Verkäufer:** *Ja, hier. Sie kostet fünfundvierzig Euro.* — Yes, here. It costs €45.
- **Kunde:** *Das ist zu teuer. Haben Sie etwas Billigeres?* — That is too expensive. Do you have something cheaper?

📎 Key phrases to remember:
- **Ich möchte ...** — I would like ... (politer than *ich will*)
- **Haben Sie ...?** — Do you have ...? (polite form)
- **Kann ich Ihnen helfen?** — Can I help you?

notes.heading: The Accusative Case — an Introduction
notes.body:
When you buy, wear, or see something, that thing is the direct object — and in German the direct object often changes its article. This is called the **accusative case**.

The big change happens with masculine words: **der → den** and **ein → einen**:

| Nominative (subject) | Accusative (object) |
|---|---|
| der Pullover | den Pullover |
| ein T-Shirt | ein T-Shirt (no change — neuter) |
| die Jacke | die Jacke (no change — feminine) |
| der Rock | den Rock |

💡 Worked examples:
- *Ich kaufe den Pullover.* — I buy the jumper. (der → den)
- *Ich kaufe eine Hose.* — I buy a pair of trousers. (feminine — no visible change)
- *Sie trägt einen Mantel.* — She wears a coat. (ein → einen)

⚠️ Common mistake: *Ich kaufe der Pullover.* If the Pullover is the thing being bought, it must be **den**.

✅ Check: only masculine nouns change in the accusative. Feminine, neuter, and plural stay the same.

notes.heading: Colours and Opinions — Describing Clothes
notes.body:
Add colour and opinion words to make your shopping sentences richer:

| German | English |
|---|---|
| rot / blau / grün | red / blue / green |
| schwarz / weiß / grau | black / white / grey |
| gelb / lila / rosa | yellow / purple / pink |
| schön / hässlich | beautiful / ugly |
| modern / altmodisch | modern / old-fashioned |
| gemütlich / bequem | cosy / comfortable |

💡 Worked examples:
- *Das rote Kleid ist sehr schön.* — The red dress is very beautiful.
- *Ich finde die grauen Schuhe altmodisch.* — I find the grey shoes old-fashioned.

📎 Key point: **Ich finde ...** + adjective is an easy way to give your opinion: *Ich finde den Mantel zu teuer.* — I think the coat is too expensive.

notes.heading: Invitations and Making Plans
notes.body:
Shopping is more fun with friends. Invite someone and make a plan:

- *Hast du Lust, mit mir einkaufen zu gehen?* — Do you fancy going shopping with me?
- *Kommst du mit ins Kaufhaus?* — Are you coming along to the department store?
- *Wann treffen wir uns?* — When shall we meet?
- *Um drei Uhr vor dem Einkaufszentrum.* — At three o'clock in front of the shopping centre.

Answers:

| German | English |
|---|---|
| Ja, gern! | Yes, gladly! |
| Gute Idee! | Good idea! |
| Leider kann ich nicht. | Unfortunately I can't. |
| Vielleicht ein anderes Mal. | Maybe another time. |

💡 Worked example: *— Kommst du morgen mit in die Stadt? — Ja, gern! Wann treffen wir uns? — Um elf Uhr vor der Bäckerei.*

⚠️ Common mistake: forgetting **mit** in *Kommst du mit?* — on its own, *Kommst du?* just means "Are you coming?", while *Kommst du mit?* means "Are you coming along (with me)?".

flashcards.example: Die Hose kostet zwanzig Euro. — The trousers cost twenty euros.
Ich kaufe ein blaues T-Shirt. — I am buying a blue T-shirt.
Die Schuhe sind sehr bequem. — The shoes are very comfortable.
Im Winter trage ich einen warmen Pullover. — In winter I wear a warm jumper.
Wie viel kostet die Jacke? — How much does the jacket cost?

flashcards.definition: I would like ... — the polite way to ask for something
flashcards.example: Ich möchte eine Hose, bitte. — I would like a pair of trousers, please.

flashcards.definition: Do you have ...? (polite form, to a shop assistant)
flashcards.example: Haben Sie das Kleid in Rot? — Do you have the dress in red?
Der Mantel ist teuer, aber die Mütze ist billig. — The coat is expensive, but the cap is cheap.
Am Samstag gehen wir ins Einkaufszentrum. — On Saturday we go to the shopping centre.

flashcards.definition: to go shopping — a separable verb
flashcards.example: Meine Mutter kauft am Freitag ein. — My mother goes shopping on Friday.
Die Schuhe sind im Sonderangebot. — The shoes are on special offer.
Sie trägt einen roten Rock. — She is wearing a red skirt.

questions.explanation: Die Hose is the trousers. Shoes are die Schuhe, the jacket is die Jacke, and the dress is das Kleid.

questions.stem: How do you ask "How much does the T-shirt cost?"
choices: Wie teuer ist ein T-Shirt kaufen?
questions.explanation: The standard question is Wie viel kostet ...? — literally "How much costs ...?".
Teuer means expensive and zu means too — so the sentence complains that the price is too high.

questions.stem: Which is the polite way to ask for something in a shop?
questions.explanation: Ich möchte (I would like) is the polite form. Ich will (I want) and the imperative Gib mir! sound rude to a shop assistant.
Der Pullover is masculine and here it is the direct object (the thing being bought), so the accusative case changes der to den.

questions.stem: "Sie trägt einen Mantel." — What does this mean?
questions.explanation: Tragen means to wear, and einen Mantel is the accusative of ein Mantel (ein → einen for masculine nouns).
German prices are said without "and": drei Euro fünfzig = three euros fifty = €3.50.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly uses the separable verb einkaufen?
choices: Wir kaufen ein am Samstag nicht.
questions.explanation: Einkaufen is separable: the prefix ein splits off and goes to the end — Wir kaufen am Samstag ein.

questions.stem: Complete the dialogue: "— Kommst du morgen mit in die Stadt? — _____ Wann treffen wir uns?"
questions.explanation: The second speaker asks when they will meet, which only makes sense after accepting — so the answer is Ja, gern! (Yes, gladly!).

questions.stem: "Ich finde die grauen Schuhe altmodisch" means:
choices: I think the grey shoes are old-fashioned
I find the grey shoes in the shop
I think the green shoes are modern
I buy the grey shoes today
questions.explanation: Ich finde ... + adjective expresses an opinion (I think/find ...), grauen means grey, and altmodisch means old-fashioned.

questions.stem: Which of these sentences is correct in the accusative case?
questions.explanation: Der Mantel is masculine, so in the accusative ein becomes einen: Ich kaufe einen Mantel.

questions.stem: Which item does NOT change its article in the accusative? "Ich kaufe _____."
questions.explanation: Only masculine nouns change in the accusative (der → den, ein → einen). Das Kleid is neuter, so it stays das Kleid.

questions.stem: A shop assistant says: "Guten Tag! Kann ich Ihnen helfen?" The best reply is:
choices: Ja, ich möchte eine blaue Jacke, bitte.
questions.explanation: Kann ich Ihnen helfen? (Can I help you?) invites you to say what you want — Ich möchte ... (I would like ...) is the natural, polite reply.

questions.stem: "Haben Sie das Kleid in Größe 38?" — The customer is asking:
choices: whether the dress is available in size 38
questions.explanation: Größe means size, and Haben Sie ...? means Do you have ...? — so the customer is asking for the dress in size 38.
Das Sonderangebot is the special offer — a reduced price. Im Sonderangebot means on special offer.
